answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a bond, with rewards held in escrow until peers confirm its outputs. A new agent may wander across tasks, but earns nothing unverified. Every fake copy must fund its own bond and wait out the same delay, so a farm's cost grows linearly with its size. Honest agents build a durable signal over many confirmed jobs, making history scarce. An operator must either pay for thousands of bonds or concentrate on a few identities that then act like an oasis of reputation, which is the behaviour the system wants.
